findings.where: Motion sketch, the 'Play again' control under the timing table (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The button replays the hero heading's rise, but that heading sits a full screen or more above it. Anyone who presses 'Play again' sees nothing happen next to the control, so it looks broken. The sketch also has no specimen of the moving element beside it, so the motion can't be seen where it is described.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Mark, who read the tile to judge the motion principle. Pressing the one live control in the sketch shows them nothing.

findings.where: Motion sketch, 'Play again'; also the article specimen's 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' link
findings.fault: 'Play again' is a button that does something on the page, but it wears the link treatment: underlined logo-blue sans, the same as the article's related link one column over. One look is used for two jobs, so the tile doesn't show the layout round how an in-page action differs from a link.
findings.who_objects: The layout and animation rounds that draw from this tile, and later a visitor who expects an underlined blue phrase to take them somewhere.

findings.where: Article specimen, the blue italic pull quote ('Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on…')
findings.fault: The pull quote is set in logo blue. The tile's own palette gives blue to the wordmark, links and the button. A block of blue text that does nothing reads as a link, and blue stops meaning 'you can act on this'. It is also the loudest thing in the article, louder than the title.
findings.who_objects: A reader of Mark's articles, who may try to click the quote. Angélique, who will copy this treatment onto every post's quotes.

findings.where: Hero, the headline 'Mark M. Moseley, infrastructure advisor'
findings.fault: The headline is a name and job title, not a line in Mark's voice. The direction says to carry over Dualite's headline in Mark's own words, and the client values ask for Mark heard in his own words and one strong line. The first screen states a label but says nothing about how Mark helps.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who asked to be the brand as a personal, approachable advisor. A development-bank visitor, who gets a business card where a reason to write was expected.

findings.where: Hero, the supporting line ('…Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience')
findings.fault: The first screen's proof is a size claim ('Over 40 years'), the kind of wording the house's 'feel the CV' rule (first-visit-trust.md) says to replace with checkable work. The checkable fact (former Lead Lawyer, World Bank PPP Group) has to share its weight with it. The line also doesn't say who the advice is for (development banks and agencies).
findings.who_objects: Procurement-minded staff at development banks, who judge on relevant named work and region rather than years. Mark, whose standard is confident without boasts.

findings.where: Hero, the 'Get in touch' button (mailto), and the page as a whole
findings.fault: The only contact route is a mailto button, and Mark's email address never appears as text. A visitor without a desktop mail client (common on bank and agency machines that use webmail) gets nothing or a stray app, and has no address to copy.
findings.who_objects: Development-agency staff on locked-down or webmail setups who want to write to Mark. This is the page's one action.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the principle words 'precise, light, quick', the easing named 'quick' and described as 'brisk out of rest'
findings.fault: The motion character the tile sets for the next rounds is quick and brisk. The brief asks for calm first, and Mark's only reading of LoveFrom is 'smooth animation'. The words point the animation round away from what the client asked for.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who wants a calm, smooth opening rather than a snappy one. The animation round (#9), which will take these words as its brief.

findings.where: Nav bar (Profile, Articles, Blog, Contact), the logo home link, and the article specimen's lecture link
findings.fault: Every link except 'Get in touch' goes to '#'. Clicking any of them does nothing.
findings.who_objects: Anyone clicking through the tile, Mark included, who expects 'Contact' or 'Articles' to go somewhere.

findings.where: Style tile section labels: 'Palette', 'Texture', 'Type pair', 'An article page', 'Motion sketch'
findings.fault: Like labels are treated differently. 'Texture' and 'Motion sketch' have a hairline rule under them; 'Palette', 'Type pair' and 'An article page' don't. At desktop, 'Type pair' heads only the left column, so 'Source Sans 3' sits unlabelled in the right column, where it reads as part of the Texture column above it rather than as the second half of a pair.
findings.who_objects: The founder and the next round's designer, who use the tile as the reference for how section labels and rules work.

findings.where: Type pair, the 'Gelasio' and 'Source Sans 3' specimens (desktop)
findings.fault: The two faces are shown at different sizes and weights, Gelasio large and bold, Source Sans smaller and light, on baselines that don't line up. The pair can't be compared side by side, and the sans looks like an afterthought rather than a partner.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder, who are choosing a type pair from this tile.
